projects.name: My CV Website
projects.description: A futuristic, interactive portfolio featuring a 3D space environment, AI chat assistant, and a hidden retro terminal OS.

caseStudy.problem: Standard static portfolios fail to demonstrate complex engineering skills or personality. I needed a platform that could serve as both a resume and a live demonstration of modern frontend capabilities.
caseStudy.solution: I built a 'living' application using the Next.js 16 App Router. It features a persistent 3D background (R3F), a context-aware AI agent (Groq Llama 3.3), and a fully functional CLI terminal Easter egg that mimics a retro OS.

architecture.description: Built on Next.js 16 (React 19) for server-side rendering and SEO. Content is managed via Sanity CMS for real-time updates without redeployment. The 3D scene runs in a separate React Context to persist across page navigation.

technicalChallenges.title: Persistent 3D Scene Navigation
technicalChallenges.description: Preventing the heavy Three.js canvas from reloading on route changes required lifting the Canvas into a global Context provider and using Next.js template files to handle page transitions smoothly over it.

technicalChallenges.title: AI Context Injection
technicalChallenges.description: The AI chat needs to know about my resume without hallucinating. I implemented a RAG-lite system that injects structured JSON data from the Sanity backend into the LLM's system prompt at runtime.

codeSnippets.title: AI Route Handler (RAG)
codeSnippets.description: Server-side route handler that constructs a context-aware prompt for the AI using live portfolio data.

codeSnippets.title: Retro Terminal Command Parser
codeSnippets.description: A custom hook-based CLI engine that handles command history, 'sudo' easter eggs, and localized output.

projects.name: OmniComment
projects.description: A decentralized commenting system allowing users to comment on any webpage via a Chrome Extension.

caseStudy.problem: Traditional comment systems are siloed to specific websites. Users cannot discuss content on static pages or sites that have disabled comments.
caseStudy.solution: A browser-agnostic overlay system that injects a discussion layer over any URL, synchronized via WebSockets for real-time interaction.

architecture.description: The system utilizes a Monorepo architecture separating the Server, WebApp, and Chrome Extension packages. Real-time updates are handled via Socket.IO adapted with Redis for horizontal scaling.

technicalChallenges.title: Chrome Extension Context Isolation
technicalChallenges.description: Managing authentication state between the background service worker, content scripts, and the injected IFrame required a robust message-passing interface to ensure secure token handling without exposing them to the host page.

technicalChallenges.title: Recursive Comment Threads
technicalChallenges.description: Storing and retrieving arbitrarily deep comment threads efficiently in MongoDB required complex aggregation pipelines using $graphLookup to avoid the N+1 query problem.

codeSnippets.title: MongoDB Recursive Aggregation
codeSnippets.description: An aggregation pipeline used to fetch top-level comments and efficiently graph-lookup all nested replies in a single database query.

codeSnippets.title: CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)
codeSnippets.description: Automated quality gates ensuring strict linting (Biome) and build verification across the Monorepo workspaces before any production deployment.
codeSnippets.code:
name: Continuous Integration

jobs:
  quality-checks:
    name: Lint, Format & Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run Biome Checks
        run: npx biome check .

      - name: Build All Workspaces
        run: npm run build --workspaces --if-present
